question.text: Will the Bundestag pass the 2027 German federal budget before 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Yes if, before 2027 CET, the German Bundestag passes the Budget Act for fiscal year 2027 in its final reading.
question.fine_print: This question will resolve based upon credible sources. In the case of ambiguity, the [Bundestag Plenarprotokolle](https://dip.bundestag.de/suche?f.wahlperiode=21&f.typ=Dokument&f.herausgeber_dokumentart=Bundestag-Plenarprotokoll&rows=25&sort=verteildatum_ab) or other official sources may be used.

research:
The final vote is scheduled for 2026-11-27. Nothing has settled the question yet, but no source I found suggests the timetable will slip.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-10: I did not fetch the DIP Plenarprotokolle search page from the question. The final vote is set for 2026-11-27, so no plenary protocol can show it yet. The Bundestag's official timetable page is the main source:
- Bundestag timetable: committee final session (Bereinigungssitzung) on Thursday 12 Nov 2026. Second reading Tue 24 to Fri 27 Nov. Third reading and recorded roll-call final vote on the Budget Act on **Friday 27 Nov 2026**. [bundestag.de](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2026/kw34-haushalt-2027-ablauf-1187766)
- The Federal Audit Office (Bundesrechnungshof) also gives 12 Nov 2026 as the date of the final committee session. [bundesrechnungshof.de](https://bundesrechnungshof.de/veroeffentlichungen/einzelplananalysen-2027)

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. The government draft has been through first reading (8 to 11 Sep 2026) and committee work. Committee work still to come: the 12 Nov final session (expected to run into Friday morning), with the 2027 budget accompanying act (Drucksache 21/7860) also finalised that day. [bundestag.de hib](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-1231740)
- The plenary vote is planned for 27 Nov, which leaves about 5 weeks of slack before the 31 Dec deadline. Under the procedure, the Bundesrat's later role does not affect this question, which only needs the Bundestag's final reading.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-09: Coalition talks between CDU parliamentary leader Frei and SPD parliamentary leader Miersch on Monday produced no agreement. Handelsblatt says the plastic tax will probably not come in 2027. [Handelsblatt](https://www.handelsblatt.com/politik/deutschland/finanzpolitik-plastiksteuer-duerfte-2027-wohl-doch-nicht-kommen/100266545.html); [t-online](https://www.t-online.de/nachrichten/deutschland/innenpolitik/id_101519006/haushalt-2027-frei-erklaert-die-geplante-plastiksteuer-fuer-tot.html)
- 2026-11-09: Bild, as reported by news.de, says the parties disagree on 10 measures worth more than €10bn combined, with a Thursday deadline. Disputed items include the plastic tax, sugar tax, housing benefit (Wohngeld) and electricity tax. [news.de](https://www.news.de/politik/860171131/zoff-um-bundeshaushalt-2027-in-der-schwarz-roten-koalition-union-gegen-plastiksteuer-plaene-zu-zuckersteuer-wohngeld-stromsteuer/1/)
- 2026-11-09: The Federal Employment Agency expects to need a bigger federal loan in 2027 than the €5.2bn planned. [Handelsblatt](https://www.handelsblatt.com/politik/deutschland/darlehen-arbeitsagentur-braucht-mehr-geld-vom-bund/100268389.html)
- 2026-11-09: The Federal Audit Office says a €6.756bn draw from a reserve in the draft no longer exists. It wants consolidation proposals by the committee's final session. [severint.net](https://www.severint.net/2026/11/09/haushalt-2027-ruecklage-entnahme-bundesrechnungshof/)
- 2026-11-08: ZDF reports the open gap is about €2bn if all four disputed measures are dropped without offsetting funding. CDU/CSU demands worth about €10bn (electricity tax cut, cold progression) are expected to be left out. The coalition aims to finish "in the next few days". There is no mention of a delay to the vote. [ZDF](https://www.zdfheute.de/politik/deutschland/bundeshaushalt-verhandlungen-schwarz-rote-koalition-streit-finanzierung-100.html)
- 2026-07-06: Cabinet approved the 2027 draft budget, about €555bn in spending. [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/markets/europe/german-cabinet-approves-2027-draft-budget-hikes-defence-investment-spending-2026-07-06)

## 4. Base rates
- 2025-11-28: The same coalition passed the 2026 budget on schedule in a roll-call vote, 322 yes to 252 no. [Ärzteblatt](https://www.aerzteblatt.de/news/bundeshaushalt-2026-vom-bundestag-beschlossen-6d4997b2-b814-4eac-ae57-e4c28a629ceb); [ZDF](https://www.zdfheute.de/politik/deutschland/haushalt-2026-abstimmung-100.html)
- From memory, not checked in this session: in years without an election or crisis, the budget usually passes in late November or early December. Examples: 2020 budget (Nov 2019), 2021 budget (Dec 2020), 2023 budget (Nov 2022).
- Exceptions:
  - 2024 budget: slipped to February 2024 after the Constitutional Court debt ruling of Nov 2023, which came days before the committee's final session.
  - 2025 budget: passed only in September 2025, after the coalition collapsed in Nov 2024.
  - 2022 and 2018 budgets: delayed by elections.
- So roughly, delays have come from a coalition breaking up, an election, or a court shock, not from ordinary arguments over budget items.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket "Will CDU/CSU-SPD German federal coalition break before 2027?": Yes 8%, No 92% (2026-11-10). This is related, since a coalition break is the main route to a delay, but it is not the same question.
- I found no market on the German 2027 budget itself on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus. The Kalshi markets on France's budget (enact by year end 46%, Article 49.3 62%) cover a different country and say nothing direct about Germany.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- By 2026-11-11/12: the coalition needs to settle the disputed items (plastic tax, sugar tax, Wohngeld, electricity tax, pension subsidy cut) before the committee's final session.
- 2026-11-12/13: committee final session (Bereinigungssitzung) on the budget and the accompanying act.
- Mid-November (not confirmed): the November tax revenue estimate, usually published before the committee's final session.
- 2026-11-24 to 27: budget week in the plenary, with the third reading and final vote on 27 Nov.
- Main risks:
  - The coalition breaks up.
  - The committee's final session is postponed.
  - A legal shock similar to the November 2023 ruling.
  - The governing majority fails to hold in the roll-call vote. The 2026 budget passed with 322 votes.
- If 27 Nov slips, December sitting weeks (dates not checked) could still allow passage before 2027.

## Research brief: will the Bundestag pass the 2027 federal budget before 2027?

The Bundestag's own timetable puts the final vote on 27 November 2026, which leaves about five weeks of slack before the deadline. The coalition is fighting over several tax measures, but no source I found expects the vote to slip.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-10: I did not query the DIP Plenarprotokolle search page. The final vote has not happened yet, so no protocol could show a result.
- The Bundestag's official timetable for the 2027 budget [source](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2026/kw34-haushalt-2027-ablauf-1187766):
  - First reading: 8 to 11 September 2026.
  - Budget committee meetings: 23 September to 11 November.
  - Final committee session to settle the budget ("Bereinigungssitzung"): 12 November.
  - Second reading: 24 to 27 November.
  - Third reading and recorded-name final vote on the Budget Act: Friday, 27 November 2026.
- 2026-11-06: A Bundestag committee notice (hib 906/2026) confirms the final debate is planned for the sitting week of 23 to 27 November. On the Thursday, the committee holds its final session, likely running into Friday morning, and also concludes its work on the Budget Accompanying Act 2027 (21/7860). The government draft is Drucksache 21/7300. [source](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-1231740)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The budget is still in committee, with the final session due Thursday 12 November.
- Draft figures: core spending of €555.4bn and new borrowing of €118.7bn. [source](https://www.t-online.de/nachrichten/deutschland/innenpolitik/id_101519006/haushalt-2027-frei-erklaert-geplante-plastiksteuer-fuer-tot.html)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-09: CDU/CSU parliamentary leader Thorsten Frei on ZDF: "We are not doing the plastic tax." The SPD insists the tax was agreed in the coalition committee and says the Union must show by Thursday how it would close the budget hole. Environment Minister Carsten Schneider (SPD) is pressing the Union too. [source](https://www.berliner-zeitung.de/article/plastiksteuer-frei-lehnt-ab-koalitionsstreit-um-haushalt-10579142), [source](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/politik/plastiksteuer-schneider-fordert-union-vor-haushaltstermin/70479489)
- 2026-11-09: Bild, via news.de, reports disagreement over ten measures worth more than €10bn, with a Thursday deadline. [source](https://www.news.de/politik/860171131/zoff-um-bundeshaushalt-2027-in-der-schwarz-roten-koalition-union-gegen-plastiksteuer-plaene-zu-zuckersteuer-wohngeld-stromsteuer/1/)
- 2026-11-09: The Federal Employment Agency expects to need a larger federal loan for 2027 than the €5.2bn planned in June. [source](https://www.handelsblatt.com/politik/deutschland/darlehen-arbeitsagentur-braucht-mehr-geld-vom-bund/100268389.html)
- 2026-11-09: Severint reports the Federal Audit Office calls the reserve behind a planned €6.756bn withdrawal empty and recommends deleting the item. I did not verify this independently. [source](https://www.severint.net/2026/11/09/haushalt-2027-ruecklage-entnahme-bundesrechnungshof/)
- 2026-11-08: ZDFheute lists the disputed items [source](https://www.zdfheute.de/politik/deutschland/bundeshaushalt-verhandlungen-schwarz-rote-koalition-streit-finanzierung-100.html):
  - Plastic tax: about €670m in 2027.
  - Sugar tax: about €690m, expected to go ahead.
  - Union demands: an electricity tax cut (about €5bn a year) and a fuller offset of inflation-driven tax creep (about €5bn), neither funded.
  - SPD demand: stop the Wohngeld (housing benefit) cuts and the abolition of the child supplement, about €770m.
  - A possible €2bn cut to the federal pension subsidy.
  - Net 2027 room is only about €1.4bn. The article says nothing about the vote slipping.
- Earlier: Bild reported at least 24 Union MPs opposing the plastic tax. [source](https://www.heidelberg24.de/politik-und-wirtschaft/plastiksteuer-24-abgeordnete-der-union-blockieren-koalitionsplan-zr-94541894.html)

### 4. Base rates
These dates are from my own memory, not checked against sources in this session:
- 2026 budget: passed 28 Nov 2025 by this same CDU/CSU-SPD coalition, on its planned schedule. [process page](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2025/kw36-haushalt-2026-ablauf-1105582)
- 2025 budget: not passed before 2025. The governing coalition collapsed on 6 Nov 2024 and the budget passed in September 2025.
- 2024 budget: the planned early-December 2023 vote was postponed after the Constitutional Court's debt-brake ruling on 15 Nov 2023. It passed in early February 2024.
- 2023 budget: passed 25 Nov 2022.
- 2021 budget: passed in December 2020.
- 2020 budget: passed in late November 2019.
- 2022 budget: a post-election year, passed mid-2022.
- Pattern: outside election years, budgets with a scheduled late-November vote usually pass that week. The two misses in recent years both came from shocks: a coalition collapse and a court ruling.

### 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket, "Will the CDU/CSU-SPD coalition break before 2027?": 8% Yes, 92% No. This is related, since a collapse would be the main route to failure.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on the German 2027 budget itself. The Kalshi markets on France's 2027 budget (46% enacted this year; 62% on use of Article 49.3) are about France and do not match this question.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-11: Budget committee session.
- 2026-11-12/13: Final committee session, the deadline for the coalition deal (plastic tax, electricity tax, tax-creep offset, Wohngeld, pension subsidy). The Budget Accompanying Act is also finalised that day.
- 2026-11-24 to 27: Second reading, including the general debate on the Chancellor's budget.
- 2026-11-27: Planned third reading and final vote.
- Sitting weeks in December would give room for a fallback vote if things slip. I did not confirm the December sitting calendar.
- Main risks: the coalition failing to agree on Thursday, a coalition breakdown, or a court or debt-brake shock.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About seven weeks remain until 31 Dec 2026. For Yes, the Bundestag must pass the Budget Act 2027 in its third reading before 2027 CET. The final vote is scheduled for Friday 27 Nov 2026. The committee's final session (Bereinigungssitzung) comes first, on 12-13 Nov.

(b) If nothing changed, the official timetable holds and the budget passes on 27 Nov. That is a Yes, with about five weeks of slack for a December fallback vote.

(c) The reference class is German federal budgets with a scheduled late-November or early-December vote, outside election years and without a coalition already in crisis. Examples are the budgets for 2020, 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2026, plus earlier years. They passed on time in roughly 85-90% of cases. Misses came from shocks:
- the 2023 debt-brake ruling by the Constitutional Court
- the coalition collapse in Nov 2024

Ordinary disputes over budget items have not caused misses. Base rate: about 88%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The Bundestag timetable and hib notice of 2026-11-06 confirm the final vote on 27 Nov.
- The same coalition passed the 2026 budget on schedule on 2025-11-28, by 322 votes to 252.
- ZDF on 2026-11-08 put the disputed gap at only about €2bn and quoted the coalition aiming to finish "in the next few days". It mentioned no delay.
- Polymarket on 2026-11-10 gives only 8% that the coalition breaks before 2027.

Evidence for No:
- On 2026-11-09, Frei said "we are not doing the plastic tax", and the SPD insists the tax was agreed.
- Bild reports ten disputed measures worth more than €10bn.
- The Federal Audit Office says a €6.756bn reserve draw is empty.
- The Federal Employment Agency needs a larger federal loan.
- Earlier reports said 24 Union MPs oppose the plastic tax, which suggests some risk to the majority in the roll-call vote.

(e) No scenario: the dispute over the plastic tax and pension subsidy escalates, and the final committee session is postponed. Coalition trust then breaks down, the SPD or Union walks out, and the vote slips into 2027 under provisional budget management.

Yes scenario: the coalition drops the plastic tax, closes the gap with global spending cuts and accounting changes, finishes the committee session on 13 Nov, and passes the budget on 27 Nov with a margin similar to 2025.

(f) I start from 88%. I move up because the timetable is firm, the same coalition delivered on time last year, the disputed sums are small relative to a €555bn budget, and there is December slack. I move down slightly for the coalition-break tail risk and for possible defections in the roll-call vote. The 8% coalition-break market overstates the relevant risk somewhat, because a break after 27 Nov would not matter. Final estimate: about 93%.

Probability: 93%

(a) About seven weeks remain, with resolution around 1 January 2027. For Yes, the Bundestag must pass the Budget Act 2027 in its third and final reading before 2027 CET. The vote is currently scheduled for Friday, 27 November 2026, after the committee's final session (Bereinigungssitzung) on 12 to 13 November.

(b) If nothing changes, the official timetable runs as planned. The committee settles the budget on 12 November and the Bundestag passes it on 27 November. The status quo points to Yes.

(c) Base rate: German federal budgets in non-election years with a scheduled late-November or early-December vote.
- Passed before year end: 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2026 budgets.
- Missed: 2024 budget (Constitutional Court ruling) and 2025 budget (coalition collapse).
- That is roughly 4 of 6 in recent years. Going back further, nearly every non-election year passed on time, so the base rate is about 85 to 90%.
- Both misses came from big shocks, not from ordinary disputes over individual items.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - The Bundestag timetable and the hib notice of 6 November confirm the 27 November final vote.
  - That leaves about five weeks of slack, and December sitting weeks could serve as a fallback.
  - The same coalition passed the 2026 budget on schedule on 28 November 2025, by 322 to 252.
  - ZDF (8 November) puts the remaining gap at only about €2bn and does not mention any delay.
  - Polymarket gives only an 8% chance that the coalition breaks before 2027.
- **For No:**
  - On 9 November, Frei declared the plastic tax dead, and the SPD insists on it.
  - Bild reports ten disputed measures worth more than €10bn, with a Thursday deadline.
  - The Federal Audit Office says a €6.756bn reserve draw is empty.
  - The Federal Employment Agency needs a bigger loan than planned.
  - These add fiscal holes just before the committee's final session.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** The talks fail and the committee's final session is postponed. The dispute over the plastic tax and pension subsidy escalates into a coalition crisis, the SPD or Union walks out, or a legal challenge to the reserve draw forces a rework. The vote slips into 2027 and the government runs on provisional budget management.
- **Yes:** The coalition drops the plastic tax, keeps the sugar tax, and closes the gap with global under-spending assumptions and a smaller pension subsidy. The committee finishes on 13 November and the Bundestag passes the budget on 27 November.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 88%. The specific evidence is mostly favourable: the timetable is confirmed, there is ample slack, and the coalition breaks with a low market probability of about 8%. The disputes are typical end-game haggling over small sums relative to €555bn. The new holes (the empty reserve and the larger Federal Employment Agency loan) add some risk, but these are usually papered over. A delay without a coalition break is possible, but December sitting weeks give room to recover. I move up slightly, to about 92%.

Probability: 92%

**(b) Status quo:** The process is on track. First reading and committee work are done, and the official timetable gives a 27 Nov final vote. If nothing changes, the answer is Yes.

**(c) Base rate:** The reference class is German federal budgets with a scheduled late-November vote in non-election years, from about 2010 to 2025. Around 85-90% passed before year end. The two misses were:
- 2024 budget: the Constitutional Court debt ruling in 2023.
- 2025 budget: the coalition collapsed in Nov 2024.

Both were large shocks, not ordinary disputes over individual budget items.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**

  - Union backbenchers are rebelling against the plastic tax.

**(e) Scenarios:**
- **No:** The plastic tax and Wohngeld dispute escalates. The committee's final session is postponed and then a new financing shock hits, such as a legal challenge to the reserve or the debt instruments. The coalition fractures and the vote slips into January.
- **Yes:** The coalition drops the plastic tax, makes small cuts and accounting changes to cover about €2bn, holds the committee session on 12-13 Nov and passes the budget on 27 Nov.

**(f) From base rate to final probability:** I start at about 88% from the base rate. I move up because the timetable is fixed, there is a big buffer, the gap is small compared with a €555bn budget, and the market prices the main failure route (a coalition break) at only 8%. Even a break would not stop passage in every case. I move down slightly for the unresolved dispute and the Federal Audit Office's warning about the reserve. That leaves me at about 93%.
